text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: runtime-pool-ggpu high OOM rate detected across us-west-2. 78% of paged-allocator slabs showing fragmentation > 70%.

maria (oncall): saw this spike ~2m ago. Customers hitting latency spikes and some 500s. Investigating. Any recent deploys?

sam (eng-runtime): no deploys in last 30m from runtime team. I'm seeing repeated CUDA driver warnings and kernel timeouts in node logs: 
```
E CudaDriver: cudaErrorUnknown at seq 14523: cuLaunchKernel failed: out of memory
W Runtime: kv_cache allocation failed, attempted 128MB commit
I Allocator: paged-slab: free_regions=12 used_regions=78 fragmented_regions=61
```

jing (infra): infra alerts show node flaps on ggpu-12, ggpu-15 in the same AZ. kubelet restart events correlated. Could be OOM kill on systemd side then node rebooting, or NV driver crash.

support (pager): customer-impact: several production requests returned 500/504; support tickets from 3 enterprise customers. Notified CSMs.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigation options? We should reduce traffic to the affected pool and failover to reserve pool. Also consider disabling prefix/KV caching temporarily to free up KV working set.

sam (eng-runtime): agree. Plan: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes to move pods off 2) scale up reserve pool (dedicated-fallback) and route traffic 3) bump eviction aggressiveness on KV cache 4) restart runtime on drained nodes after restart of nvidia-driver.

ops-bot: runbook step triggered by maria: `./runbooks/paged-oom.md -> page_oncall`

maria (oncall): executing step 1 now: `kubectl cordon ggpu-12 && kubectl drain ggpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sam (eng-runtime): applying a temporary eviction tweak: `redwoodctl config set runtime.kv.eviction_threshold 0.55 --cluster=us-west-2` — reduces cache residency. Will monitor.

jing (infra): also increasing node pool autoscaler min from 4->6 to give headroom. `gcloud container clusters update ... --min-nodes=6`

support (pager): routing rule applied: 20% traffic shifted to dedicated-fallback pool. Notifying customers of degraded performance.

maria (oncall): logs after eviction tweak (1m): fragmentation dropped to 59% but OOMs still present on two nodes, nvdriver stack traces present.

sam (eng-runtime): looking at heap dumps: KV cache leak pattern — slow accrual of stale page references on certain attention paging paths, causing fragmentation to creep until allocator can't satisfy new KV pages. I have a patch candidate to free stale page references more aggressively but it's risky mid-incident.

maria (oncall): don't merge patch live. We can continue mitigation: 1) keep traffic shifted 2) restart runtimes on flapping nodes after driver reload 3) temporarily disable attention paging for models with longest context lengths (reduce max_seq_len to 2048)

sam (eng-runtime): starting a canary rollout of reduced max_seq_len on staging then prod fallback flag `--enable-paged-attn=false` for the heavy models. Doing canary on 2 pods in fallback pool.

ops-bot: deploy bot: canary applied to fallback pool (pods runtime-rt-5, runtime-rt-7).

maria (oncall): customer-impact update: support reports 40% of requests to affected endpoints still see 500s, but latency on remaining requests improved after traffic shift.

jing (infra): running `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv` on afflicted nodes shows steady memory usage with occasional huge spikes. Driver logs show `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:xx:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.` suspects kernel-driver interaction.

sam (eng-runtime): action: for nodes where driver crashed, let's mark them `NoSchedule` and reprovision with updated driver. I'll prepare a driver-reload playbook: `ansible playbook reload-nvidia.yml --limit ggpu-12,ggpu-15`

maria (oncall): doing that now. Restarting runtime service after driver reload.

maria (oncall): quick health: after draining and eviction tweak + 20% traffic shift, error rate down 60% and fragmentation trending down. No new node flaps in last 5m.

support (pager): messaging sent to affected customers: incident in progress, we have mitigations applied and will follow up with RCA.

sam (eng-runtime): note for follow-up RCA: investigate paged-attention allocator's region coalescing logic — it appears small stale references prevent coalescing leading to long-term fragmentation. Also correlate with GPU driver resets that leave KV page mappings orphaned.

jing (infra): for remediation: replace driver on nodes older than kernel 5.10, ensure driver and kernel compatible, and add a watchdog to restart runtime if NV driver emits Xid 79.

maria (oncall): summary for postmortem: root symptoms — slow KV/paged-attn fragmentation + occasional NV driver resets -> allocator fragmentation -> OOM -> node flaps -> customer impact. Mitigations applied: traffic reroute to fallback pool, eviction threshold increased, nodes drained and driver reloaded, temporary disable for paged-attn on heavy models. Next steps: collect heap dumps, kube events, driver logs; schedule postmortem and assign owners (sam: runtime bugfix; jing: infra driver rollout + watchdog; maria: incident writeup + customer comms).

support (pager): confirmed owners. I'll create a ticket and link to this thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> P2, monitoring for recurrence for 6h.

maria (oncall): leaving on-call notes: escalate to eng-runtime if errors spike again, otherwise handover at shift end. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

sam (eng-runtime): adding logs/artifacts link: https://weblogs.redwood.internal/1932109876/dumps and a short trace: `stacktrace: alloc_paged_region -> mark_stale_ref -> fail_coalesce`

ops-bot: runbook step completed: mitigation checklist ticked.

maria (oncall): handing over to night oncall. last check 1932110376, leaving thread for postmortem prep.
